title: Cyclic shear and damage evolution of pile–silty clay interface under CNL/CNS conditions
content:
by Shaoning Wang, Chien-Ta Chen

To clarify the cyclic shear response and damage evolution mechanism of pile–silty clay interfaces, this study conducted a series of large-scale cyclic direct shear tests combined with numerical simulations to investigate the effects of interface texture width, soil moisture content, shear displacement amplitude, normal stress, and loading mode on the mechanical behavior of the interface. Two normal boundary conditions, including constant normal load (CNL) and constant normal stiffness (CNS), were considered. The cyclic shear stress–displacement hysteresis behavior, volumetric deformation characteristics, shear stiffness degradation, equivalent damping ratio evolution, and energy dissipation characteristics were analyzed. The results show that the interface shear strength follows the Mohr–Coulomb failure criterion. Increasing the interface texture width enhances the initial shear resistance compared with the smooth interface, although the peak shear strength does not increase monotonically with texture width. Increasing the soil moisture content from 9% to 15% reduces the initial peak shear strength by 48.9%, while increasing the normal stress from 100 to 300 kPa increases the initial peak shear strength by 164.2%. The interface shear stiffness and equivalent damping ratio exhibit a three-stage evolution pattern consisting of rapid degradation, gradual transition, and stable convergence during cyclic loading. The stiffness degradation mainly occurs during the early loading stage and gradually stabilizes after approximately 25 cycles. The cumulative dissipated energy is affected by boundary conditions and loading parameters. Compared with CNL conditions, CNS conditions reduce the cumulative dissipated energy by approximately 19.7%, while increasing interface roughness and normal stress enhances the energy dissipation capacity. An improved Mohr–Coulomb constitutive model incorporating cyclic damage evolution was established by introducing a damage variable to describe the degradation of interface mechanical parameters. The proposed model was implemented in ABAQUS and validated using cyclic shear tests under different moisture contents. The numerical results reproduce the main trends of experimental shear stress–displacement response and normal deformation evolution under different moisture-content conditions, with R² values ranging from 0.836 to 0.852 for the normal displacement–cycle relationships.
